column1:
The FOMC’s November 2017 statement is moderately upbeat on growth and employment, noting hurricane-related disruptions but continued strengthening in the labor market and a gradual policy path amid soft core inflation. The October 2017 Beige Book adds tempered nuance: across the Richmond, Atlanta, and Dallas Districts, Hurricanes Harvey and Irma disrupted activity and exacerbated already-widespread labor shortages—especially in construction and transportation—leading to stronger wage pressures yet also restraining some business growth and recovery efforts. While retail/household spending increased in several districts, the combination of labor constraints and storm effects points to modest headwinds alongside pockets of inflation pressure. Net result: still positive, but a touch less upbeat than the FOMC statement alone, consistent with staying accommodative and proceeding gradually.
